## What

Papercusp can be extended **from inside the running system**: an agent declares a new
**datatype** (a named entity TYPE) or a new **tool** (a capability), and the platform
treats it as first-class — no engineer, no redeploy. The point: a domain (an internal
reference app was the first) models its own concepts *on* the self-improvement substrate instead of building a bespoke
system beside it. Design anchors D-001..D-011 (the plan); the decisive ones are inlined below.

## Datatypes — the extension flow

`meta:define-datatype` (`agent-tools/datatypes/declare.ts`) writes one row to
`harness_shared.datatype_registry` (migration 421) via `datatype-registry-store.ts`.
Authority is **dedup-only** (D-010, the npm/crates model): a hard unique id (the kebab slug,
the PK) + a soft semantic gate (`findSimilarDatatypes` — `title_tsv` lexical fused with the
`embedding` cosine leg; `force:true` overrides). Declaration also requires/validates:

- **A self-improvement surface (P-010, `datatype-self-improvement.ts`)** — `checkSelfImprovementForDeclare`
  REQUIRES `{ improvements[], scorecard[], gym{signals,rubric} }` for the authoritative tiers
  (generic-kind / first-class); a datatype is self-improvable *by construction*. Projection is exempt.
- **A compilable `payload_schema`** — `isCompilableSchema` (ajv) rejects a malformed schema at declare
  time, so the create path never has to fail-open.

Once a **generic-kind** datatype is declared, its `work_item_kind` is live everywhere with **zero
bespoke plumbing**:

- **Create + validate** — `work_items:create { kind, payload }` accepts the kind
  (`work_items/_create-core.ts` → `getGenericKindDatatype`) AND validates `payload` against the
  datatype's `payload_schema` (`validateDatatypePayload`, ajv) → `invalid_payload` on a violation. This
  is the *validation* a datatype exists to provide (a malformed `bet` is rejected, not stored as a blob).
- **Visibility** — `featureFamilyKindClause` (`work-items.ts`) makes the kind appear in
  list / count / search.
- **Placement (OPT-IN)** — `frontierPlacementKindClause` (`datatype-frontier-placement.ts`) enrols the
  kind in the autonomous cup-placement frontier ONLY when the datatype carries the `pot-placement` tag.
  Visibility ≠ placement: a datatype is a data SHAPE; auto-spawning a worker per instance is deliberate.
- **Blueprint dependency** — a blueprint's `dependencies.datatypes` resolves against the registry:
  `depHostSetsFromCatalog(cat, listRegisteredDatatypeNames(sql, ws))` populates `availableDatatypes`
  (a `Set`, not an array), gated at harness creation (`agent-tools/harness/create.ts`).

### Tiers (D-002 / D-008)
`generic-kind` (default — a work_item kind + validated payload, zero migration) · `first-class` (a native
SQL-backed concept — its migration ships through the **PR rail**, NOT runtime) · `projection` (read-only,
an EXTERNAL engine is the single writer, `authoritativeWriter:'engine:<name>'` — Papercusp holds a view,
runs no gym over it).

## Tools — the extension flow (D-003: safety = confinement + review, not prohibition)

`meta:define-tool` (`agent-tools/tools/define.ts` → `define-tool-router.ts`) routes by tier:

- **composed** → registers LIVE as a `code_recipe` (a DAG over EXISTING tools; mints no new capability),
  invoked via `recipes:run`.
- **sandboxed-imperative | elevated** → NEVER registered at runtime; `tool-scaffold.ts` emits a reviewable
  `defineTool` skeleton (writes/runs/mints nothing — a `not_implemented` stub) for the PR rail
  (`tools:scaffold` → review + adversarial confinement proof → `platform:contribute`).

`dynamic-tool-confinement.ts` is the **per-dynamic-tool envelope** (P-003 core, adversarially proven):
`deriveDynamicToolEnvelope` holds ONLY the declared caps/paths/domains, NARROW-ONLY vs the host role, and
can never hold the minting/escalation floor (`DYNAMIC_TOOL_FORBIDDEN_CAPABILITY_GLOBS`:
grant/revoke/envelope/set-tier/meta:define-*/tools:scaffold/platform:contribute/secrets/processes:kill/cup:spawn).
The runtime PEP wiring of this into dispatch is a **capability-TCB** edit (`capability-envelope/**`,
`tier:'human'`, D-007) → reviewed PR rail, never an unattended auto-apply.

## Gotchas (these bite)

- **`payload_schema` is `Set`-vs-array etc. — types matter.** `DependencyHostSets.availableDatatypes` is a
  `Set<string>` the resolver `.has()`-checks; passing an array compiles-via-esbuild but fails tsc + crashes
  the resolver. Always `npx tsc -p packages/operator-core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` (esbuild ≠ typecheck).
- **The minimal work-items test schema must carry `datatype_registry`.** The visibility + placement clauses
  reference `harness_shared.datatype_registry`; `test/_work-items-schema.ts` (`HARNESS_FEATURES_CONSOLIDATED_DDL`,
  used by `createFreshPgDb` tests) includes a minimal version so those tests don't fail
  `relation ... does not exist`. `createOrgTestDb` tests apply the full migration 421.
- **Don't blind-build the gated parts.** first-class migration CODEGEN, the runtime confinement PEP wiring,
  and the **Comb-published shared tier** (a data-carrying Cupboard listing + the server moderation/distribution
  worker at `/admin/cupboard-moderation`) are PR-rail / cross-component by design — an operator-core-only build
  would be a non-functional stub.

## Live-verified end-to-end (2026-06-30, running operator)

Exercised against the live operator via loopback MCP (scratch workspaces, cleaned up):

- **Datatype loop:** `meta:define-datatype {tier:'generic-kind'}` → `work_items:create {kind}` with a VALID payload returns `ok:true`
  (the instance lands in `harness_features_consolidated` as a feature-family row); an INVALID payload is rejected `invalid_payload`
  with the ajv message. A generic-kind create requires an in-scope **harness** (by design — the feature table is harness-keyed).
- **The `createWorkItem` re-check.** `work_items:create`'s gate validated the generic kind, but `createWorkItem` (a second entry point)
  re-checked `isWorkItemKind` and refused the insert — fixed (`work-items.ts` now re-checks the registry via `hasGenericKind`).
- **Observability spans new datatypes (P-011).** `curation:state-of-pot` and an UNFILTERED `work_items:list` both surface a generic-kind
  instance. The **kind-FILTER** path was the gap: `work_items:list`/`work_items:search` locked `kind` to a `z.enum` of built-ins, so you
  could not filter the queue by a declared datatype — relaxed to a free string (built-in OR registered generic-kind); `familyOf()` already
  routes it to the feature family. Unknown kind simply lists empty.
- **Tool loop:** `meta:define-tool {tier:'composed'}` registers a `code_recipe` LIVE; `recipes:run` then executes it (the system gains AND
  uses a tool from inside). `meta:define-tool {tier:'elevated'}` emits a review-gated scaffold file (NOT registered at runtime).
- **Dogfood witness:** `platform:dogfood_verify {prUrl}` is read-only and wired — it returns the 5-stage round-trip assertion
  (prTracked / reviewed / merged / shipped / linked) with precise gaps.
- **Gap on the outward PR path (WI-1293):** `platform:enable` on an install that already has a legacy shared harness returns
  `selfHive.status:'already_standing' detail:'legacy_shared_harness'` and does NOT stand up the dedicated `papercusp-platform-pot`
  member checkout, so `platform:contribute {kind:'pr'}` fails `self_hive_not_found`. Only blocks the owner-gated/cred-gated live
  fork→PR step; the internal loop + dogfood verifier are proven.
